cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-sgl_p4e7; S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-sgl-p4e7/a494f23c-12c7-42b3-bd29-e8fda110136c/scratchpad; for f in videos/*.mp4; do b=$(basename $f .mp4); ffmpeg -loglevel error -i $f -vf "scale=1:1,fps=1" -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 $S/$b.raw & done; wait; python3 -c "
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
im=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float)
row=im[100]
# find stripe extent
cols=[i for i in range(row.shape[0]) if row[i].sum()>0]
row=row[cols[0]:cols[-1]+1]
def rs(a,n): 
  x=np.linspace(0,len(a)-1,n); return np.array([np.interp(x,np.arange(len(a)),a[:,c]) for c in range(3)]).T
B=rs(row,200)
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
  v=np.fromfile('$S/'+L+'.raw',dtype=np.uint8).reshape(-1,3).astype(float)
  V=rs(v,200)
  print(L,len(v),np.abs(B-V).mean().round(1),np.corrcoef(B.sum(1),V.sum(1))[0,1].round(2))
"

content.text:
The barcode matches option F, Maroon 5's "Sugar." I turned each of the ten videos into a barcode the same way (one average color per second), stretched them all to the same length, and compared each one with barcode.png.

| Video | Average color difference (lower is closer) | Brightness correlation (higher is closer) |
|---|---|---|
| **F. Maroon 5 - Sugar** | **13.6** | **0.76** |
| G. Uptown Funk | 29.7 | 0.21 |
| J. On the Floor | 36.8 | 0.10 |
| Others | 44.5 to 129.2 | -0.20 to 0.21 |

F is the closest match on both measures, and by a wide margin. The next-best video is more than twice as far off in color, and no other video's brightness follows the barcode's pattern.

Answer: F
